canonical_question: What specific criteria in the JMatPro Ni-alloys database led to the design target of keeping TCP phase fraction below 1 vol%?

question_variants.question: What specific criteria in the JMatPro Ni-alloys database led to the design target of keeping TCP phase fraction below 1 vol%?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document confirms that the 1 vol% TCP threshold was a design target achieved by adjusting refractory additions using the JMatPro Ni-alloys database. It does not specify the underlying physical or chemical criteria within the database model that dictated this specific 1 vol% boundary.

answers.answer: The JMatPro Ni-alloys database simulation was used to design the HESA alloy with the aim of keeping the fraction of TCP phases less than 1 vol% by adjusting refractory additions.
answers.conditions: CALPHAD-based simulation using JMatPro Ni-alloys database
answers.measurement_outcome: TCP fraction designed to be < 1 vol%
answers.mechanism: Adjustment of refractory additions during simulation to meet TCP phase fraction target
answers.boundary_limitation: Simulation is design-assisted; actual achieved values not reported in this section.
evidence_spans: The design of HESA was also assisted by CALPHAD-based simulation (JMatPro [55] , Ni-alloys database), and the aim is to contain more than 60 vol% of strengthening L1 2 γ′ as commercial Ni-based superalloys.

Furthermore, since the addition of refractory elements can easily promote the formation of detrimental topological-close packed (TCP) phases, the fraction of TCP was designed to be less than 1 vol% while adjusting the refractory additions.

source_evidence_spans: the fraction of TCP was designed to be less than 1 vol% while adjusting the refractory additions.
